title: Libet's 1983 readiness-potential experiment
summary: The Brain paper reports cerebral activity before the reported moment of conscious intention.
body: Benjamin Libet, Curtis A. Gleason, Elwood W. Wright, and Dennis K. Pearl, "Time of conscious intention to act in relation to onset of cerebral activity (readiness-potential)" (Brain, 1983), reported brain activity preceding the clock-time at which subjects said they had decided to move. The v1 article says the lead was about 300 milliseconds. That number was not re-read from the paper, so it is not stored. The experiment is about a finger movement in a lab, not about whether a person is responsible for a life plan. What the timing means is disputed. Schurger, Sitt, and Dehaene later offered an accumulator model that does not read the early signal as a decision.
